This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 4: Ghost in the Machine.
A personal AI agent that lives on my NAS instead of someone else's cloud. Four moving parts:
Home hardware
OpenClaw, an open-source agent harness, in a container on a UGREEN DXP2800: quad-core Intel N100, 8 GB of RAM, one NVMe SSD and two hard drives that already spent their days doing backups.
A soul made of files
The agent has no memory of its own, every model is a blank page. What makes it someone is a folder of plain-text files: rules, personality, my profile, its daily notes. It re-reads its own papers before answering, like a séance that consults the script before summoning anything.
Work while I sleep

articles.description:
Most "AI for finance" demos have the same flaw: the model writes a confident paragraph full of numbers, and nobody can tell which of them came from the ledger and which the model made up.

**[OfinTech Desk](https://github.com/OfinTech/ofinTech-Dask)** is our answer to that, and as of **v1.0.0 (27 Oct 2026)** it is fully open source under **Apache-2.0**. It's a desktop app (plus an optional self-hosted Team Server) that reads your ledger, spreadsheets, documents and inbox, does the arithmetic *in code*, fills in your own Excel and Word files with a source for every figure, and asks a human before it sends or changes anything.

This post is not a feature tour. It's a walk through the engineering decisions inside the engine, the places where we think the design is interesting, and the places …

Don Norman's forcing function (Lockton 2009, Eight design patterns for errorproofing):
A forcing function is a design element that prevents you from completing an action…

articles.author: Peter W.
articles.description:
Every "add vector search" proposal comes with the same promise: users phrase questions their own way, keyword search misses, and embeddings fix it. A feature request on Synthadoc made that case for us (issue #411):
Synthadoc uses BM25 exclusively. For wikis under ~200 pages, BM25 is fast and precise; at 500+ pages, paraphrase and concept queries increasingly miss without a semantic layer.
It also asked us to turn embeddings on by default. That's a big change for a pip-installed tool (more on the cost below), so before writing any retrieval code we built a benchmark to answer three questions:
Does BM25 really get worse at paraphrased questions as a wiki grows?
Does the vector search we already ship (off by default) fix it?
If not, what design would and by how much?
Yes, keyword search degra…
articles.title: Should our LLM wiki use vector search? We benchmarked it before deciding

articles.author: CyberMax
articles.description:
The game in one paragraph


Sled Volt is a three-lane sled runner down an endless snowy mountain: change lanes, jump, tuck, grind rails, fill a frost meter and double-tap for VOLT to smash through everything, while a snow beast called the Rimehorn chases you after a stumble. It ships twice: a free browser game (three.js) and a Roblox game with live races of up to 8 players.
The whole game rule set is a deterministic 60 Hz simulation: core.js in the browser and Sim.luau on Roblox, ported line for line. Same seed and same inputs give the same course, the same collisions and the same score. A generated parity spec runs recorded inputs through both and compares every tick, so a change in one language that isn't mirrored in the other fails the build.
The course generator always keeps one lane p…
articles.title: How we built one sled racing game for Roblox and the browser

articles.author: Ioneyrezende
articles.description:
Tailworm: eleven unfixed flaws in a mesh VPN, and the SSH path that carries root


A mesh VPN is usually deployed so that nobody has to publish an administrative interface. Tailscale builds a tailnet out of WireGuard peer-to-peer links, and headscale reimplements the control server for teams that want to run it themselves. That design removes public load balancers and open ports, which is why so many engineering teams treat the tailnet as an internal network with a login attached. A security audit published this week argues that the login is doing more work than the operators think.
Cyberdione Labs reported eleven vulnerabilities in Tailscale 1.104.2 and in the self-hosted headscale v0.29.5 control server. The researchers grouped them under the name Tailworm and released the details public…
articles.title: Tailworm: eleven unfixed flaws in a mesh VPN, and the SSH path that carries root

Its 101 landmarks are pins on India's outline, coloured by kind: temples and shrines, forts and palaces, tombs and memorials, and civic and engineering works. Beside the map is a list grouped by state that narrows as you type. Pick a place and the map gives way to a 3D model you can orbit, zoom and step through with the arrow keys. Each monument also has its own address, such as #taj-mahal, so a link can open a model directly. Opening on the map was the most important design choice. Most people know the Taj Mahal is in Agra, but fewer could place Rani ki Vav, Ramappa or Key Monastery. Se…
